title: Phase 4 · Stage 12: Repositories and LINQ
summary: Put storage behind repository interfaces, hand them to the Library, and replace hand-written loops with LINQ queries.

steps.title: Storage behind an interface
body: `Library` creates its own `Catalog` and lists with `new`, so it is welded to in-memory storage. Phase 6 will save to files and Phase 9 will run inside a web server. The fix is a **repository**: an interface that says what storage can do, and a class that does it one particular way.
var library = new Library(today, new InMemoryBookRepository(), new InMemoryMemberRepository(), new InMemoryLoanRepository());
The Library asks for the interfaces in its **constructor**; whoever creates it decides which implementations to pass. This is *dependency injection* by hand, and Phase 8 will let a container do it.
With storage handing out sequences, most loops become **LINQ** pipelines:
var byYear = books.OrderBy(b => b.Year).ThenBy(b => b.Title, StringComparer.Ordinal);
Each method takes a **lambda** (`b => ...`): a tiny function applied to every item. Read `Where(b => b.AvailableCopies > 0)` as *keep the books that have a copy in*.

steps.prompt: Match each loop to the LINQ call that replaces it.
pairs: add up a number from every item
is there at least one item that ...?
turn every item into something else
the first item that ..., or null
steps.explain: Each name says what the loop was for, which is the main reason LINQ code is easier to read than the loop it replaces.

code: var books = new List<(string Title, int Year, int In)>
var titles = books.Where(b => b.In > 0).OrderBy(b => b.Year).Select(b => b.Title);
steps.explain: Dune is filtered out (no copies in), the rest are sorted by year, and only titles come out of `Select`.

steps.prompt: Arrange the pipeline: Fiction books with a copy in, newest first, as titles.
steps.explain: Filter, sort, project. The two `Where` calls could swap without changing the result, and that order is accepted too; but `Select` must come last, because after it there are only strings, with no `Year` to sort by.

steps.title: Repositories, and LINQ instead of loops
prompt: 1. **Repositories.** Replace `Catalog` with three interfaces and their in-memory classes:
interface IBookRepository   { bool Add(Book book); Book? Find(string isbn); IReadOnlyList<Book> All(); }
interface IMemberRepository { void Add(Member member); Member? Find(int id); IReadOnlyList<Member> All(); }
interface ILoanRepository   { void Add(Loan loan); void Update(Loan loan); IReadOnlyList<Loan> All(); }
`InMemoryLoanRepository.Update` replaces the loan with the same `Id` (throw `KeyNotFoundException` if there is none).

2. **Library.** Its constructor becomes `Library(DateOnly today, IBookRepository books, IMemberRepository members, ILoanRepository loans)`. It exposes `Books`, `Members`, `Loans`, `Book? FindBook(string isbn)` and `IEnumerable<Book> Search(string text)` instead of `Catalog`. Inside, use LINQ (`Any`, `Count`, `FirstOrDefault`) instead of loops, and `_loans.Update(...)` to record returns and renewals.
3. **Top level.** Create the library with the three in-memory repositories. Use LINQ in `Stats`, `Fines`, `Loans`, `Info` and `MemberInfo` (*last borrowed* is `LastOrDefault`).

- `list by-title`, `list by-author` (then title) and `list by-year` (then title) sort the list; titles and authors sort **ordinally**. `list` alone keeps insertion order. Anything else: `Error: use list [by-title|by-author|by-year]`.
- `available` lists books with at least one copy in, or `Nothing is on the shelf.`
5. `help`: `Commands: add, list, available, find, info, shelve, status, authors, join, members, member, lend, return, renew, loans, policies, today, advance, fines, pay, stats, fine, help, quit`.

hints: Turn `Catalog` into `InMemoryBookRepository : IBookRepository` (drop `Search`, it moves to `Library`). The member and loan repositories each wrap a `List`.

In `Library`, keep the interfaces in private readonly fields set by the constructor. `ActiveLoanCount` is `Loans.Count(l => l.IsActive && l.MemberId == memberId)`; the active loan lookup is a `FirstOrDefault`. Return and renew save with `_loans.Update(loan)`.
Sorting: `library.Books.OrderBy(b => b.Year).ThenBy(b => b.Title, StringComparer.Ordinal)`. Make `FormatBooks` take an `IEnumerable<Book>` and call `ToList()` once inside.
